purpose: Selpercatinib is used to treat certain types of cancer that have a specific genetic change called a RET alteration. It can be used for non-small cell lung cancer, thyroid cancer, and other solid tumors that have this mutation. Your doctor will test your tumor to see if this medication is right for you.
how_it_works: Inside cancer cells, a protein called RET can get stuck in the 'on' position, telling cancer cells to keep growing out of control. Selpercatinib works like a targeted off-switch that blocks this overactive RET protein. By blocking RET, the medicine helps slow down or stop the cancer cells from growing and spreading.
common_side_effects: Dry mouth, diarrhea, constipation, tiredness, swelling in your hands or feet, high blood pressure, changes in liver blood tests, nausea, headache, and rash. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to keep an eye on these.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious liver problems, so your liver will be checked with blood tests regularly. It can also cause high blood pressure, heart rhythm changes (QT prolongation), allergic lung reactions, and bleeding. It may harm an unborn baby, so use reliable birth control during treatment and for a period after. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as many drugs can interact with selpercatinib.
typical_dosing: The typical dose is 160 mg taken by mouth twice a day (morning and evening). You can take it with or without food. Swallow the capsules whole and try to take them at the same times each day. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless your next dose is within 6 hours — in that case, just skip the missed dose.
